extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and researchers studying enumerative combinatorics and hyperplane arrangements; readers solving advanced textbook exercises
extracted.subtask_description: Working through advanced enumerative combinatorics and hyperplane-arrangement exercises: proving identities, applying Möbius inversion, using deletion–contraction, verifying freeness/truncation properties, and deriving generating-function/exponential-formula consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kalai condition for g-vector factorization (equation 3.142)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let Δ be a finite simplicial complex (equivalently, an order ideal I of B_n). Suppose that for any face F of dimension at most k−1 (including the empty face of dimension −1) the link of F is acyclic (i.e., has vanishing reduced homology). Let f_i denote the number of i-dimensional faces of Δ. Then there exists a simplicial complex Γ with g_i i-dimensional faces such that ∑_i f_i x^i = (1+x)^{k+1} ∑_i g_i x^i.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is stated as a special case of a result of Kalai (Theorem 4.2). Note the text remark that the hypothesis here is stronger than in the present exercise; references and stronger conjectures (Stanley, Kalai) are given. Use this condition as a sufficient topological hypothesis guaranteeing the stated factorization of the f-polynomial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stanley partitioning conjecture (Conjecture 2.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let L be the poset (or meet-semilattice) of faces of Δ. Conjecturally there exists a partitioning of L into intervals [s,t] of rank k+1 such that the bottom elements s of the intervals form an order ideal of L.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is Stanley's stronger conjecture; the case k=0 is proved and some generalizations exist (Duval, Duval & Zhang). The conjecture provides a combinatorial (interval-partition) criterion stronger than Kalai's homological hypothesis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of chromatic polynomial via Möbius inversion
rubrics_metrics.description: For a partition σ of V let χ_σ(n) count maps f:V→[n] that are constant on blocks of σ and distinct on different blocks. For any partition π of V, χ_π(n) = ∑_{σ ≥ π} n^{#σ} μ(π,σ). In particular χ̂0(n) = χ_G(n), giving an interpretation of χ_G(n) in terms of Möbius functions (Rota).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the lattice of partitions and Möbius inversion to express the chromatic polynomial; this perspective links colorings to partition-poset Möbius values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Isomorphism of intersection poset of graphical arrangement with connected partitions
rubrics_metrics.description: For graphical arrangement B_G (hyperplanes x_i − x_j = 0 for edges ij of G), the intersection poset L(B_G) is isomorphic to the set of connected partitions of G ordered by refinement. Consequently χ_G and χ_{B_G} differ at most by a power of q, and equality follows since both have degree equal to #V.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify intersections of selected hyperplanes with connected components of the spanning subgraph; then apply earlier results to relate graph- and arrangement-polynomials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deletion–contraction identity for chromatic polynomial (equation 3.119)
rubrics_metrics.description: For an edge e = {u,v} of G, χ_G(n) = χ_{G\e}(n) − χ_{G/e}(n): number of proper colorings of G equals number of proper colorings of G\e minus number of proper colorings of G/e (those with u and v forced equal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combinatorial proof: count colorings of G\e and subtract those where endpoints of e receive the same color (which correspond to proper colorings of the contraction G/e). This is standard deletion–contraction reasoning; references provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recurrence for number of acyclic orientations (ao)
rubrics_metrics.description: For an edge e of G, ao(G) = ao(G\e) + ao(G/e), with initial condition ao(G) = 1 if G has no edges. In constructing orientations o1 and o2 by adjoining u or v to an acyclic orientation of G/e, exactly one of o1,o2 is acyclic except in ao(G/e) exceptional cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the bijective orientation-construction argument and reference Stanley (Discrete Math. 1973) for justification. This recurrence parallels the chromatic deletion–contraction but with sum rather than difference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regions of graphical arrangement correspond to acyclic orientations
rubrics_metrics.description: A region of the graphical arrangement B_G is obtained by specifying for each edge whether x_i < x_j or x_i > x_j; such a specification is consistent iff the resulting orientation is acyclic. Hence the number of regions r(B_G) equals ao(G).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides a geometric/combinatorial bijection (Greene & Zaslavsky). Use this to translate between arrangement-region counts and graph orientation counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Whitney's theorem for characteristic polynomial of arrangement
rubrics_metrics.description: For an arrangement A in K^n, χ_A(x) = ∑_{B ⊆ A, central} (−1)^{#B} x^{n − rank(B)} (Proposition 3.11.3/Whitney).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply Whitney's theorem to decompose arrangement characteristic polynomials by central subarrangements; used in conjunction with exponential formula techniques in this chapter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of exponential formula for labelled combinatorial classes (equation 3.144)
rubrics_metrics.description: For sequence χ_n(x) arising from arrangements decomposed into connected components (partitions), their exponential generating function satisfies ∑_{n≥0} χ_n(x) z^n / n! = exp( ∑_{n≥1} c_n(x) z^n / n! ), leading to factorization χ_n(x) = c_n x for some integers c_n and further combinatorial consequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translate decomposition of structures into exponential formula; set suitable x-values to solve for component generating functions A(z), B(z) when needed (see exercises 112–113).

rubrics_metrics.name: Finite-field method to evaluate characteristic polynomials / region counts
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate χ_A(q) by counting points in finite field complements or using enumerations mod p for large primes p (Theorem 3.11.10 and examples: Catalan arrangement, Linial/threshold arrangements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose a large prime p and count tuples over F_p satisfying avoidance conditions; apply Theorem 3.11.10 and Exercise 1.34 when appropriate. References: Athanasiadis, Postnikov, Stanley.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freeness criterion for arrangements via supersolvability
rubrics_metrics.description: If the intersection lattice L of an arrangement is supersolvable then the module of derivations Ω is free (Stanley, Jambu & Terao). Conversely, freeness need not follow from other properties; freeness/nonfreeness examples and open questions are discussed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Terao's removal theorem and induction on number of hyperplanes; see Orlik–Terao and Terao's work for precise statements and exceptions. Several open/famous problems cited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counting injective linear maps over finite fields via Möbius inversion (exercise 119)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let N(V,X) be number of injective linear transformations V→X (finite field). Let F=(W) count linear maps with kernel containing W; by Möbius inversion N(V,X) = ∑_{W'} F(W') μ(0,W'), leading to explicit q-binomial sums: N(V,X) = ∑_{k=0}^n (−1)^k q^{k(k−1)/2} [n choose k]_q x^{n−k}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Count by summing over possible kernels and invert with Möbius function on subspace lattice. Use q-binomial coefficients and known Möbius values (equation (3.34)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recurrence and generating function for subsets without k consecutive integers
rubrics_metrics.description: Let f(i,n) be number of i-subsets of [n] with no k consecutive integers. The recurrence (by largest omitted element) yields a bivariate generating function F(x,y) with an explicit rational form; parity/congruence consequences follow (exercise 121).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derive recurrence by analyzing the largest omitted element and sum to get rational F(x,y); evaluate specializations (e.g., x=−1) to obtain periodic vanishing properties modulo 2k+2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poset factorization and L_w = J(P_w) criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: For a word w factorized as g_{i1}⋯g_{ik} z, define P_w as the multiset of indices with specified partial order; then L_w (a certain lattice) equals J(P_w) (order ideals of P_w). Conversely, Pw being an antichain is equivalent to w being product of distinct commuting generators, giving [ε,w] boolean iff that holds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Cartier–Foata monoid / trace monoid theory and linear extension arguments (connections to Knuth and Viennot's heaps). This gives a combinatorial/poset criterion for structure of intervals in the monoid-lattice context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partitionability and R-labelability / shellability implications
rubrics_metrics.description: If a finite poset L admits an R-labeling (or is shellable/Cohen–Macaulay in certain settings), then L is partitionable: it admits a partition into intervals [r(K),K] where r(K) is defined via descent conditions on labels. Some converses/questions remain open (Stanley's conjecture on partitionability of Cohen–Macaulay posets).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct r(K) from an R-labeling by locating indices where label decreases; use chain/interval containment to show partitionability. References: Björner, Garsia, Stanley, and others; technical 0-Hecke-algebra characterization discussed (McNamara).

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparability graph determines order polynomial (flip/autonomous-subset transformation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Two finite posets P and Q have the same comparability graph iff there is a sequence P = P0, P1, …, Pk = Q where each step dualizes (turns upside-down) an autonomous subset T (a subset with no comparabilities to its complement in certain directions). Consequently Ω_P(m) = Γ_P(m) depends only on the comparability graph Com(P).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Either use sequence of dualizations or an explicit mapping between order-preserving maps to show the order polynomial depends only on the comparability graph. References: Dreesen–Poguntke–Winkler, Kelly, Stanley.

rubrics_metrics.name: Barycentric subdivision preserves Euler characteristic / µ invariance
rubrics_metrics.description: For poset Q arising from barycentric subdivision of P (Q_0 in text), µ_Q(ˆ0,ˆ1) = µ_P(ˆ0,ˆ1), reflecting that a finite simplicial complex and its barycentric subdivision are homeomorphic and have equal Euler characteristic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Proposition 3.12.1 and combinatorial counting of multichains to show equality of µ-values; applies to face lattices of polytopes and related structures.
